signals.title: AUD/NZD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Policy Divergence
signals.text: AUD/NZD trades sharply higher following dual policy shocks overnight. The G10 scorecard records AUD as the primary leader with a 1W average of +0.960% across 4 pairs, while NZD lags the G10 at -0.627% across 4 pairs, generating an extreme bilateral spread of 1.587%. Australia's Q3 headline CPI printed firm at 1.3% q/q alongside a 1.0% trimmed mean, reinforcing hawkish expectations for RBA cash rate policy at 4.60%. In direct contrast, the RBNZ delivered a surprise rate hold at 2.75%, widening the base policy spread to 185bp in favor of the Aussie dollar. The BEER misvaluation model shows AUD/NZD rich at z=+1.87σ (spot 1.2552 vs 1.2429 fair value), indicating stretched short-term valuation, but momentum remains dictated by the active policy divergence. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/NZD; policy divergence favors upside continuation against stretched fair value. Catalyst: BoC and Fed rate decisions later today at 13:45 UTC and 18:00 UTC. Risk: RBNZ guidance indicating further tightening materializes quickly, prompting an aggressive unwinding of long AUD/NZD exposure.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.78, holding below its SMA200 at 158.49 within a tight range-bound structure. An overnight OIS differential of +270bp (SOFR 3.93% vs TONA 1.23%) anchors structural USD carry demand, but options markets are pricing aggressive protection against a spot drop. Saxo Bank 25d risk reversals show a strong put skew of -2.12, reflecting elevated demand for downside protection ahead of the BoJ policy meeting on 30 October. JPY speculative positioning in the CFTC COT report shows net short contracts trimmed by WoW +12,222 to -25,598 (pctl 94, z +1.43), indicating Leveraged Funds are reducing short exposure. While VIX at 17.5 reflects normal volatility and rules out broad safe-haven flows, options skew confirms institutional market participants are paying up for downside hedges against potential BoJ policy adjustments. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY; downside options demand hedges heavy carry positioning. Catalyst: BoJ interest rate decision on 30 October. Risk: BoJ delivers an entirely dovish hold, removing downside hedge demand and triggering a retest of 160.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Risk Premium + Positioning Crowding
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1122, remaining in an established downtrend below its SMA20 (1.1218), SMA50 (1.1423), and SMA200 (1.1575). Options metrics show 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.2%, establishing an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.3% as participants price heavy event risk into the European Central Bank and Federal Reserve decisions. CFTC COT data shows Leveraged Funds heavily short the single currency at net -94,138 contracts, positioned in the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z -1.72). The SOFR-€STR OIS spread stands at +149bp in favor of the dollar (SOFR 3.93% vs €STR 2.44%), providing persistent carry support to USD. Additionally, retail sentiment via Retail sentiment data shows an extreme 87% long positioning that directly opposes institutional spec shorts, underscoring capitulation risk on a renewed downward leg. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; monetary policy divergence and elevated options protection dominate. Catalyst: ECB rate decision on 29 October at 13:15 UTC. Risk: ECB delivers an unexpectedly hawkish hold alongside a dovish Fed stance, forcing an immediate short-covering squeeze toward the SMA20.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Policy Divergence + Technical Resistance
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4063, executing a counter-trend pullback inside a larger uptrend while testing the underside of its falling SMA20 at 1.4160 and holding above the SMA50 at 1.4015. Rates markets carry an OIS spread of +169bp favoring the greenback (SOFR 3.93% vs CORRA 2.24%), but the pair faces an immediate policy hurdle with both central banks meeting today. Leveraged Funds positioning sits short CAD at net -92,789 contracts (12th percentile, z -1.42), showing a stretched institutional short stance that leaves the Canadian dollar vulnerable to a short squeeze if domestic policy surprises hawkishly. WTI crude oil trading up +1.70% to $101.6 provides underlying terms-of-trade support to the loonie, limiting USD/CAD upside momentum. Trade bias: Range/bearish USD/CAD; short-term rally constrained by technical overhead resistance and dual rate decisions. Catalyst: BoC rate decision today at 13:45 UTC, followed by the Fed rate decision at 18:00 UTC. Risk: BoC pauses or strikes a dovish tone while the Fed signals sustained tightening, resuming the broader uptrend toward 1.4200.
